chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: First manicure and the word delicatessen
summary: The two boys were chased from a barber-shop window after watching a manicure and marveled at the word delicatessen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: The first time I'd seen a manicure. I seen this cat sittin' in a barber chair, me and my uncle. He was getting a shave and getting a haircut, and had this woman playing with his hands. So me and my uncle, we ...(?)... [LAUGHS] We were lookin' in the window...! And the woman looked at us, the barber looked at us. "What are them niggers doin'...?"

So we looked. There was no (?). So we went back home and told her what happened, this lady was playin' with the man's hand while he was in the barber shop. She said, "She was giving the man a manicure."

First time I seen the word "delicatessen." Some delicatessen. Because we were going to school and learning to read. D-e-l-i-c-a-t-e-s-s-e-n. That's a big word. Delicatessen. And all we seen was bologna and ham and cheese in the window...
